issueCommentThread.body:
Adoption blocker.

This is about Gates: the check that stands in the doorway before work is called good. A green result should mean Directive actually looked. A red result should say what to do next.

What a new person hits: The check that is supposed to prove the project definition is well formed reports "zero files, all clean" while the definition file is sitting on disk, unread.

Why that ruins the product for them: Setup's certificate of health did not look at the file it certifies. The reassurance is fake.

How likely: Medium-high. It runs as part of setup's own proof, so it is on the first-run path.

Refutation target under test (Stop 1 comment 5837066832): verify:vbrief-conformance exit 0 with a clean-zero candidate count is sufficient proof that PROJECT-DEFINITION (and its policy namespace) was inspected, so Setup Phase 2 may complete on that green alone even when PROJECT-DEFINITION is present on disk but outside the counted candidate set.

**Verdict: the refutation target does not survive.**

## Clean-zero is not inspection of PROJECT-DEFINITION
blocks-the-design
Evidence: At `042eea8c31f5629b1fc0cfa2f75e4cb967af7980`, `evaluateConformance` builds candidates from `gitTrackedFiles` / `gitStagedFiles` filtered by `isLifecycleArtifactPath`, then adds PROJECT-DEFINITION only when `options.projectDefinitionPath` is set (`packages/core/src/vbrief-validate/conformance.ts`). `runConformance` passes that option solely from `process.env.DEFT_PROJECT_PATH` (`packages/core/src/vbrief-validate/main.ts`); there is no `--project-definition` flag. On empty findings it returns exit 0 with `` `${candidates.length} vBRIEF file(s) clean -- no bare keys (#1620)` ``, so length 0 is a success shape. Local discovery mirror at that SHA: untracked `xbrief/PROJECT-DEFINITION.xbrief.json` present on disk → 0 candidates; same path with `projectDefinitionPath` injected → 1 candidate (`<configured PROJECT-DEFINITION>`); after `git add`+commit without inject → 1 candidate. Setup Phase 2 writes PROJECT-DEFINITION via `project:write-narratives` while `xbrief/active/` is empty, then runs `deft verify:vbrief-conformance --project-root <policy-project-root>` (`content/skills/deft-directive-setup/SKILL.md` Branch-policy persistence gate).
Failure mode: Fresh Phase 2 (or any tree with PD on disk but not yet tracked, or a non-lifecycle `DEFT_PROJECT_PATH` without the env wired into the conformance process) prints clean-zero exit 0 while bare keys in PROJECT-DEFINITION, including bare `plan.policy`, are never `scanVbrief`'d. Treating that green as proof the file was inspected false-certifies the #1620 doorway.
Disposition: Before bind, reject any lean that keeps "exit 0 / clean-zero ⇒ PROJECT-DEFINITION inspected." Existing mechanism to inventory first: force the resolved PROJECT-DEFINITION into the candidate set (canonical path and/or `DEFT_PROJECT_PATH`) on every Setup / policy conformance invocation, or fail closed when the resolved artifact exists on disk and was not counted. Do not invent a second Setup-only scanner while this injection seam already exists.

## Phase 2 already re-reads PROJECT-DEFINITION for the two policy keys
sharpens-framing
Evidence: Same skill block requires three postconditions before Phase 2 completion: re-read PROJECT-DEFINITION for `plan["x-directive/policy"].allowDirectCommitsToMaster`, confirm bare `plan.policy` is absent, and `verify:vbrief-conformance` exit 0, plus `policy:show` match. Stop 1 P2 collapses that into "Setup Phase 2 reads that exit 0 as proof the policy block is namespaced / PROJECT-DEFINITION was checked."
Failure mode: A lean that only restates the agent re-read, or that treats P2 as "Setup has no PD read," would either under-ship the machine #1620 hole (P1) or over-correct prose that already separates policy key checks from conformance.
Disposition: Keep P1 as the gate/mechanics gap. Narrow P2 to: conformance green is still consumed as the bare-key certificate in the Phase 2 postcondition cluster, and that certificate can green without scanning PD; the existing re-read covers only the two named policy conditions, not the full #1620 key walk. Bind the scanner/wiring fix; do not bind a Setup-prose-only restatement of the re-read as the remedy.

## Tracked canonical PROJECT-DEFINITION is already a lifecycle candidate
footnote
Evidence: `isLifecycleArtifactPath` accepts any `xbrief|vbrief/` + artifact-suffix path (`packages/core/src/layout/resolve.ts`); `xbrief/PROJECT-DEFINITION.xbrief.json` matches. Reproduction: once tracked, it appears in the candidate set with no `projectDefinitionPath` injection. Filename D7 already exempts PROJECT-DEFINITION (`isScopeLifecyclePath` is length-3 only; conformance skips D7 for configured candidates and for non-scope-lifecycle paths).
Failure mode: None for bind if the lean scopes the hole to untracked / non-injected configured paths rather than claiming canonical tracked PD is invisible to discovery.
Disposition: No separate disposition weight; use as scope guard when stating the mechanism.

Existing mechanisms inventoried before any new gate: `evaluateConformance` + optional `projectDefinitionPath`, CLI `DEFT_PROJECT_PATH` passthrough, Setup skill preserve-`$DEFT_PROJECT_PATH` / `--project-root` rules, policy writer tests that already init git then run conformance with env for noncanonical paths (`packages/cli/src/policy.test.ts`). Injection/swarm lens: not triggered — this arc concerns candidate discovery and Setup postcondition meaning; issue/comment text stayed data.

## In plain English

Setup Phase 2 can treat a green `verify:vbrief-conformance` as proof PROJECT-DEFINITION was scanned for bare keys, but the gate can exit 0 with zero candidates while that file sits on disk unscanned. The bound fix is to make every Setup/policy conformance invocation count the resolved PROJECT-DEFINITION (or fail closed when it exists and was not counted), and to stop reading clean-zero exit 0 as inspection proof. Confirming this map asserts that harvest and later implement work close that certificate hole without replacing the existing Phase 2 policy re-read.
